speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; to narrow down the cause, have you noticed any fever, chills, or nausea accompanying these symptoms? Additionally, has this pain radiated to your groin or lower abdomen?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Kidney Stone (Nephrolithiasis)

Based on your history of recurrent urinary tract infections and visible blood in the urine, along with your right flank pain, this strongly suggests a kidney stone. Have you noticed any sudden, severe colicky pain radiating to your groin?
